stanzas: vita, dulcédo et spes nostra, salve.
Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes
O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
orig.credit: Traditional (Latin text as in the Vatican's edition)

stanzas: our life, sweetness and hope, hail.
To you we sigh, groaning and weeping
show to us after this exile.
O merciful, O kind, O sweet Virgin Mary.

notes: lines 1 and 3: 'Salve' is a greeting ('hail', literally 'be well'); it opens line 1 and closes line 3.
line 8: 'Eia' is an exclamation of urging, 'come now', 'ah then'; 'advocata' is one who pleads another's case.
line 14: 'clemens' is merciful, mild; 'pia' is dutiful, loving, kind. This closing line is often said to be a later addition, sometimes credited to Bernard of Clairvaux (disputed).
